section_summary.extract_value: This discussion summarizes a single cross-sectional study that examined how body image-related cognitive fusion and body appreciation mediate the effect of body image discrepancy (controlling for BMI) on disordered eating in a sample of women from the general population. The authors report that body image discrepancy has both direct and indirect effects on eating psychopathology (via increased cognitive fusion and decreased body appreciation) and note limitations including cross-sectional design, an all-female general population sample, and reliance on self-report measures.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion reports results from the present (single) study showing that body image discrepancy and BMI are positively associated with eating psychopathology, and that body image-related cognitive fusion (increasing risk) and body appreciation (protective) mediate this relationship. Limitations noted include the cross-sectional design, exclusive use of a female general-population sample, and reliance on self-report measures.
